note: Historical measurement design from the 2026-11-17 brief. This schema and its client/collector are preserved for provenance and legacy self-tests only; they are not the current runtime and must not be enabled alongside the single active stack. Current source of truth: data/shop/measurement.json; active browser runtime: assets/measure.js; active reference collector: tools/analytics_endpoint.py. Production collection remains OFF and is not deployed, so no production event or conversion count exists.

lifecycle.reason: The repository selects one canonical five-event runtime. This older page_view/guide_view/product_click/special_link_click/nav_click schema remains only for historical provenance and legacy tests.

principles: No cookies, no localStorage profiles, no fingerprinting, no cross-site identifiers.
The browser sends no user identifier at all: no IP handling on the client, no session id, no user id.
Do Not Track and Global Privacy Control switch the tracker off entirely; Save-Data also switches it off.
Only the URL path is sent — query strings and fragments are stripped before dispatch (query strings can carry tokens).
The referrer is reduced to its host name; full referrer paths are not sent.

The endpoint must not set cookies, must not serve third-party scripts, and must aggregate rather than profile: raw request data is kept no longer than 24 hours, then only daily aggregates remain (documented retention for the reference collector).
privacy.authority: Design record of this repository. The FTC's guidance on disclosures and Amazon's Operating Agreement do not regulate analytics design; these rules are this site's own commitment, published so a reader can check the code against them.

events.when: Once per page load, after DOM ready.

fields.p: URL path, no query, no fragment

events.purpose: The denominator: how many page loads each page gets. Nothing else in this layer is interpretable without it.

events.when: On an article or guide page, once, when the reader scrolls past the halfway point of the main content.
events.purpose: Distinguishes a landed page from a read page, so the next topic is chosen from content that held attention, not only from clicks that bounced.

events.when: Click on any outbound link to an Amazon product page (amazon.com /dp/ or /gp/product/, or a link.amazon short link).

fields.p: page path where the click happened

events.purpose: Interest in a product, wherever it appears — evidence links, comparison tables, cards. Counts every outbound product link, sponsored or not, so disclosure-adjacent behaviour stays visible.

events.when: The subset of product_click whose href carries a tag= parameter — a tagged Special Link.
events.purpose: The revenue-eligible click. This is the event that can be compared against Amazon's own Associates report, which is aggregated by tag and date — never per click (0C4-F-05 explains the join limitation).

events.when: Click on an internal navigation link (site nav, front-door card, .acts button pair).
events.purpose: Which path readers take towards the comparison and the guides; correlated with product_click it shows which routes lead to action.

endpoint.contract: POST a single JSON object to the configured endpoint path, Content-Type: application/json, body exactly the event fields above. Respond 204 on accept, 400 on a schema violation, 429 when rate-limited. The endpoint sets no cookies, sends no credentials, and must not require an account.
endpoint.reference_implementation: Legacy only: tools/analytics_collector.py (standard library) implements this historical contract for its self-test. The current runtime contract is in data/shop/measurement.json and tools/analytics_endpoint.py.
endpoint.client_config: Legacy only: assets/track.js reads window.ZONE3_ANALYTICS_ENDPOINT and is not injected by current page templates. Do not configure it alongside the canonical Z3_MEASURE runtime.
endpoint.deployment_state_note: GitHub Pages is static and cannot host the endpoint. The reference collector must run on any host the owner controls (a small VM, a container, a serverless function that speaks the same contract). Until it is deployed and the endpoint URL is set on the pages, zero events are recorded — deliberately, rather than counting into the void (0C4-F-05).
endpoint.conversion_join: Amazon Associates reporting is aggregated by tag and date; it does not expose per-click identifiers. Conversions therefore join to this ledger only at tag x date x channel granularity, through the campaign ledger on campaigns.html. This layer never claims a per-visitor conversion attribution.

reader_capture.note: Reader capture (SG-30) needs a processor the owner chooses (an email list tool or the same self-hosted endpoint with a /subscribe route). No address, processor or consent wording has been supplied, so no form is shipped: a form that goes nowhere would be a dark pattern, not a feature (0C4-F-07).

search_console.note: SG-29: site verification for Google Search Console requires a token generated in the owner's Search Console account and either a meta tag or a DNS record this session cannot create. When the token arrives it goes into a <meta name="google-site-verification"> tag on every page template (0C4-F-06). The sitemap is already published at /sitemap.xml for submission on day one.
